main_text.head: EXAMEN.
main_text.p: Ego vero assumo: Atqui Abel fuit justus, quia credidit in Semen mulieris promissum, in satisfacturū [?] pro peccatis suis, in Agnum Dei ab initio mactatum, quia placuit Deo per fidem, ex qua deinde pure & innocenter vixit. Certamen fuit inter Cain & Abel (ut nonnulli ex veteribus scribunt) de hoc, quomodo & propter quid Deus hominem, qui propter peccatum reus est, respiciat, ut aestimonium consequatur, quòd sit justus coram Deo. Heb. 11. 4. Abel quidem obtinuit justificari remissione, i. e. remissione peccati. Gen. 4. 7. Idq; fide promissionis, propter semen. Heb. 11. 4. Et haec fides paulo post, Gen. 4. v. ult. declaratur: Enos coepit invocare nomen Domini.

Cain vero negavit justitiam coram Deo esse levatione seu condonationem peccati, fide propter semen: sed judicavit, se posse sacrificiis & aliis operib. peccatum levare & tollere, & quidem irascitur, DEUM ad se & sua sacrificia, propter dignitatem operum, non respicere. Gen. 4. 5. Cain non curavit levationem peccati per fidem, quia non agnovit, quale & quantū on[?] sit pecca-

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "satisfacturū" (the mark over the u is unclear); "obtinuit" in the Abel sentence is a guess for the blurred word after "Abel quidem", marked here as printed "oenfit" is illegible, so please check; "on[?]" in the last line; the page number "10" (printed as "ıo") and the catchword "tum" are uncertain. The opening "c" of the paragraph beginning "propter quid" is read as "&". The Greek-letter abbreviations and the leading "ab" of "ab initio" may be misread. The number in the far right margin is handwritten and was left out.
